gates.reason: Unit-test fixtures exercise pure accounting logic and perform no gated security operation.
Arithmetic, overlap, residual, ordering, coverage, and scope-deduplication expectations were inspected and are reproducible for the tested valid inputs.
Test-only fixtures and assertions are not runtime hot-path code.
Pure in-memory accounting code performs no authentication, filesystem, network, browser rendering, command, SQL, container, or secret operation.
Counterfactual numeric domains are not validated, allowing negative direct-dollar claims or non-finite scale fractions to corrupt savings and bill results.
Matrix assembly is linear in token entries; scope lookup is map-based, duplicate scopes are set-deduplicated, and no N× detector execution occurs.
Tests cover restricted query serialization, the viewer/server engine boundary, and authenticated-data gating without executing fixture strings.
Tests verify required envelope arrays and canonical snapshot expiry boundaries, though malformed array members are not covered.
Test-only source-contract checks are outside production hot paths.
Browser parameters are serialized with URLSearchParams from an explicit allowlist, and engine dependencies are type-only imports.
The trust-boundary parser checks only that two fields are arrays and accepts malformed recommendation and provenance members as a ready result.
The client seam has a small erased type graph, constant-sized query serialization, and no detector or engine runtime import.
The test verifies that only the already-sanitized secrets-at-rest signal is projected, using coordinates and counts rather than secret content.
Parity assertions verify every engine-consumed client-carried field is supplied and documented server-only omissions remain explicit.
Test fixture construction and parity assertions do not run in production.
The mapping passes a sanitized secrets-at-rest signal and does not read files, send LLM requests, expose OAuth credentials, or introduce an executable browser boundary.
The projection explicitly maps client-carried recommendation inputs and enumerates absent server-only artifacts without calculating or fabricating claims.
The mapping is a single shallow object projection with no loops, recomputation, or heavy runtime imports.
Dangerous command text is inert detector input inside a unit-test fixture and is never executed by this file.
The frozen broad-spread fixture enforces byte-identical recommendation output for legacy detector parity and uses a fixed timestamp for reproducibility.
Synthetic fixture generation and snapshot comparison are test-only.

findings.title: Malformed numeric counterfactuals can produce negative or non-finite accounting results
findings.what: The directUsd branch rejects only values greater than the available residual. For usd=-1 with a $1 server residual, lines 544-549 take -1, increase the residual to $2, and book a -$1 marginal. The scaleTokens branch likewise performs arithmetic without requiring a finite fraction in [0,1]; NaN passes the subsequent comparisons and is committed, making billFinal and total NaN. This violates the module's non-negative residual and faultless savings contracts.
findings.fix: Before mutation, reject directUsd unless usd is finite and non-negative, and reject scaleTokens unless every supplied fraction is finite and within [0,1]. Apply equivalent finite/non-negative validation to token and fee inputs if they are not guaranteed at ingestion.
findings.acceptance: Add tests showing negative and non-finite directUsd values and negative, greater-than-one, and non-finite scale fractions are rejected without mutation; assert billOriginal, billFinal, total, booked marginals, and category rollups remain finite and non-negative.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed there is no lower-bound or finiteness check before Math.min mutates row.server, and Math.max with NaN feeds NaN through lines 733-736 into the committed cell.

findings.title: Trust-boundary parser accepts malformed recommendation and provenance members
findings.what: parseRecommendationResult validates only that recommendations and domainCoverage are arrays. Values such as {recommendations:[null], domainCoverage:[null]} pass and are cast to RecommendationResult, allowing malformed or unevidenced claims to enter the viewer as kind=ready and potentially fail or misrepresent analysis downstream.
findings.fix: Validate each recommendation and domain-coverage member with a runtime schema, including required recommendation identity, claim/evidence provenance, severity/category fields, and valid numeric/date domains, before returning the typed result.
findings.acceptance: Add boundary tests proving null, primitive, partial, non-finite, and provenance-free members are rejected while a complete evidence-backed recommendation envelope is accepted.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read lines 69-81 and the corresponding tests; neither inspects array members, so malformed members reproducibly survive the only runtime validation.
